description: PWR-style fuel bundle: UO2/GRPH/ZIRC pin lattice (as fuel_assembly_uo2) plus two parallel absorber rod channels, one HF (long-life control) and one B4C (fast shutdown poison), side by side.
name: pwr_fuel_bundle
why: UO2 melts 2865 C and is a poor conductor (8 W/mK) so heat must leave through the ZIRC clad (22 W/mK, melts 1852 C) -- never let cladding itself approach its own melt point. HF absorbs NEUT at 95% chance per neighbour and survives coolant chemistry for a full core life (melts 2233 C); B4C absorbs at 90% with a bigger heat kick per capture (4 K vs HF's 3 K) but melts far sooner (2763 C is still high, but warms faster) -- run HF as the everyday trim rod and reserve B4C for the fast trip. Withdraw either rod (erase it) to raise flux, reinsert (redraw) to scram.
